clauses.reason: The order approves the code: "do adopt and approve the report, recommendations, and findings of the Administrator and do order that the said code of fair competition be and it is hereby approved." An approved code had legal effect through NIRA section 3 (standard of fair competition under 3(b), injunction under 3(c), misdemeanor under 3(f)). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375), approved June 14, 1935, repealed "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes". The resolution states no effective date other than its approval. That repeal removed the prospective operative effect of this command, so its first end is June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not the end, and Schechter (May 27, 1935, section 3 delegation held unconstitutional) is a validity characterization, not an end date.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued; the NIRA section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the code during the period is an accrued effect for past action only. The proviso in section 2 of the resolution limits the section 5 exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful, names agreements rather than codes and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for past action. Nothing held continues the approval after June 14, 1935.
